title: Catalog
description: The shape of catalog.yaml, the single source of truth. Nothing is installable, packageable or referenceable unless it is declared here, and `ak validate` fails on an entry with no directory and on a directory with no entry. Every entry carries a batch and a status; skills, packs, protocols, roles and references additionally carry a provenance origin, because the question 'is there a donor file behind it' has an answer for authored content and not for a schema or a profile. 'invocation' is U or M and nothing else (AGENTS.md, 'The invocation law'); 'status' moves contract -> authored; 'provenance_origin' is donor or conversation, where conversation means a G:L locator rather than a fabricated source path (plan 1.4). Profiles are install sets and adapters are host contracts: neither may name anything about which agent fills a seat.

description.description: The host-facing description, emitted into every bundle's manifest. Not package.json's description and not required to agree with it: package.json describes the npm package, this describes what the host installs. adapters/codex/CONTRACT.md section 5.2 states which identity fields are compared against package.json and which are not.

author.description: Who the host manifests name as the package's author. Emitted into every bundle's manifest as {"name": <this>}, so it is stated once here rather than per host. Not a kebab_id: it is a display name and carries spaces.

license.description: The package's SPDX licence identifier, emitted into every bundle's manifest. Must agree with package.json and with the LICENSE file the bundle carries; adapters/codex/CONTRACT.md section 5 makes that disagreement release-blocking.

skills.description: Public entrypoints. A user-invoked skill may call model-invoked skills and may never call another user-invoked skill; where a public entrypoint and a delegated phase operation both exist, they are declared as separate entrypoints rather than as an exception to the law (AGENTS.md, plan 7.1).

entrypoints.description: Present when the skill exposes more than one way in. Each names its authority from common#/$defs/authority and whether a human or a delegated controller may start it.

packs.description: Domain packs. They attach constraints and review lenses by artifact and semantics; they never start a lifecycle phase (plan 3).

activation.description: The artifacts and semantics that attach the pack, in prose here and as machine-checkable rules in the pack's own manifest (pack.schema.json). Never a file extension alone.

protocols.description: Shared phase logic, invoked by skills and never by humans.

roles.description: Role prompts, never individually invocable. 'tier' is the activation tier of a review lane, not a ladder of any other kind.

references.description: Loaded on demand, never exposed as slash commands. 'loaded_by' names the skills that may load each one, which is what keeps progressive disclosure checkable (plan 4).

schemas.description: The 31 JSON Schemas. 'common' holds the shared $defs and validates no document itself; the sixteen artifact schemas are exactly common#/$defs/schema_id, catalog, skill, pack, case, rulings, install, firstmate-binding, tracker-binding and constitution-article validate configuration rather than run artifacts, and review-event, review-pattern, episode, memory-run and learn-state validate the learning runtime's ledger records, which is why none of those carry an envelope. Schema entries have no provenance origin: they are original contracts, not adapted donor files.

policies.description: Machine-referenceable rulings. Citing a ruling is mandatory wherever a skill touches one (AGENTS.md, authoring rule 4).

profiles.description: Install sets. A profile selects which entries are installed and never names anything about which agent fills a seat (AGENTS.md).

default.description: Exactly one profile carries this, and it is the package's default_profile.

adapters.description: Host contracts. An adapter states precisely which restrictions its host actually enforces; a declaration is not enforcement (plan 1.2, 1.3).

invocation.description: U = user-invoked, only a human starts it, and the packager emits the host's manual-only key for it. M = model-invoked. There is no third value (AGENTS.md, 'The invocation law').

status.description: A contract entry is declared and not yet written; an authored entry has its body. The batch that writes the body sets it to authored.

provenance_origin.description: donor = adapted from at least one pinned donor file, each with a provenance/adaptations.yaml row donor@commit:path that exists at the pin. conversation = no donor implements it and it carries a G:L locator instead. This field answers only 'is there a donor file behind it'; mechanism-level origin lives in provenance/conversation-map.yaml (plan 1.4).

batch.description: Authoring batch. The order is deliberate and git is the resume point.

authored_entry.description: An entry whose body is authored content adapted from a donor or written from the conversation.

declared_entry.description: An entry that declares a contract of this repository's own making, so it has no donor origin to record.
